records.reason: Bromochlorobenzene under weak elution is a low-polarity compact anchor. It helps constrain baseline V1/V2 calibration while the model learns localized tails in polar families.

Ethyl cinnamate at 5/1 fills a solvent-strength gap in a conjugated ester family with measured m73 conditions such as 51de9c0ea3a29bbcda54 and a387411cbcb6be48bde4. The label can separate onset movement from completion broadening.

This high-ratio benzyl acrylate-like ester samples a less strongly interacting aromatic ester regime. It provides a transfer control for whether broad corrections from conjugated or polar esters generalize to compact ester rows.

A heavy-halogen ether at 1/1 with higher density and 150 ul provides a compact-side loading anchor. It is paired with 5004f7ec0b1a4d127095 to test ratio and loading effects within one weakly interacting scaffold.

The weak-ratio dibenzoyl-like carbonyl scaffold tests whether a polar acceptor-rich molecule can remain compact at the low-strength end. This helps localize the delayed behavior seen in measured carbonyl-rich rows.

A small aromatic diketone at 5/1 and low sample volume probes a carbonyl-rich control under moderate loading. Its label can distinguish generic acceptor-count effects from scaffold-specific endpoint tails.
This simple aryl ketone under 1/1 supplies an ordinary ketone anchor for the onset-switch hypothesis. It helps calibrate solvent response against more delayed fused or polar ketones.
A high-loading dibrominated fused aromatic provides a hydrophobic calibration point under 5/1. It constrains broad V2 corrections using a weakly interacting heavy-atom structure.
The small halogenated oxygenated molecule under 2/1 PE is a compact control at a distinct solvent family and loading amount. It broadens calibration beyond DCM-heavy observations.
This weakly interacting chlorinated alkylbenzene at 2/1 PE is an additional nonpolar anchor. It tests whether loading amount and PE conditions preserve compact elution for hydrophobic controls.
A heavy iodo-aromatic ether at 5/1 probes size and halogen effects without a donor or basic center. Its label can prevent molecular-weight-driven inflation of V1/V2 in the retrained model.

This long-chain aromatic ester at 30/1 PE tests whether a hydrophobic ester remains compact at very weak solvent strength. It is useful for learning the boundary between hydrophobicity and loading-solvent effects.
A chlorinated phenylpropyl structure at 10/1 PE is a simple hydrophobic condition probe. It complements the paired m147 row below and tests solvent-ratio transfer in a low-interaction family.
The long-chain acrylate ester at 50/1 PE samples a high-ratio hydrophobic ester regime. It can reveal whether strong solvent shifts onset smoothly in a flexible ester or produces a completion tail.
An amino-substituted aromatic ester at 1/1 PE provides a donor/basic acceptor probe at low sample volume. It tests whether the basic-aromatic failure region extends to ester-attached anilines.

High-ratio acetylnaphthalene-like material is a targeted onset-response probe. It complements measured fused ketone behavior and can teach whether V1 transitions sharply while V2 remains locally calibrated.

This is the higher-ratio, lower-volume member of the m152 heavy-halogen pair with 4c40bd6781093d65e26f. The matched scaffold contrast tests whether condition and loading changes alter endpoints together in a compact family.
An isopropyl aromatic ketone at 10/1 provides a flexible ketone control between compact simple ketones and fused ketone rows. It helps identify whether a solvent threshold is scaffold-dependent.

The stilbene-like hydrophobic aromatic with a large loading-solvent volume probes sample-introduction effects in a nonpolar structure. It provides a compact anchor for interpreting broad predicted intervals elsewhere.

A chlorinated phenylpropyl compound at 5/1 PE supplies the stronger-solvent partner for 28767818a5e0052e4f5a. This matched pair teaches local ratio sensitivity without relying on a polar functional group.
A small chlorinated carbonyl at 1/1 and 50 ul tests a low-loading ketone baseline. It helps separate ordinary onset behavior from the measured delayed carbonyl families.

Dimethyl benzophenone-like material at 1/1 and low volume probes a two-aromatic carbonyl scaffold near the known carbonyl failure region. It is structurally informative alongside measured m131 behavior such as fb65053351114fb51265.
A methoxy aromatic ester at 10/1 samples an acceptor-rich but nonbasic control. It can distinguish ester and ether effects from the severe basic-aromatic rows.
The flexible aromatic aldehyde under 10/1 PE probes solvent response in a weak donor-free family. It adds coverage of aldehyde retention without duplicating the highly polar probes.

Indene-like fused hydrocarbon under 10/1 PE provides a compact fused-aromatic reference. It helps prevent transfer of delayed corrections from polar fused structures to ordinary hydrophobic fused rings.
A neutral aliphatic diester at 0/1 PE is a compact multi-acceptor anchor. Its label tests whether acceptor count alone predicts a tail when there is no aromatic donor or basic center.

Diphenylethylene under 10/1 PE samples a hydrophobic aromatic response with no heteroatoms. It provides a clean calibration point for separating aromaticity and solvent effects from silica-specific interactions.

A secondary benzylic alcohol at 5/1 DCM probes donor-containing but flexible, moderately hydrophobic behavior. It complements measured compact and delayed donor rows and tests donor-scaffold specificity.
This m147 condition is the weaker-ratio partner of 28767818a5e0052e4f5a. The same simple hydrophobic scaffold at two PE ratios gives a useful local solvent-response slope.

Methyl anthranilate-like material at 5/1 and low volume supplies a donor/basic aromatic ester probe. It tests whether an amino group on an ester scaffold follows the severe basic-aromatic pattern or remains compact.
This second m12 condition changes the ratio and loading volume relative to 5c4c93d36b2fc71b1442. The matched pair teaches whether a fused hydrocarbon's onset shifts smoothly under PE conditions.
A low-logP hydrophobic aromatic at 20/1 PE provides another compact anchor at a different density and sample volume. It helps stabilize calibration across the high-ratio region.

hypotheses.content: Compact hydrophobic and weakly interacting rows are necessary calibration anchors because severe tails in polar families do not justify global endpoint inflation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Compact anchors constrain the retrained model's baseline V1/V2 calibration and keep local tail corrections from spreading across ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do additional weakly interacting and heavy-atom structures remain compact across PE and DCM condition ranges?

hypotheses.content: Large V2 completion tails are localized to scaffold-condition-loading neighborhoods and should be learned as endpoint-specific local corrections rather than generic polar or carbonyl offsets.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local endpoint calibration can reduce severe V2 errors while preserving compact-row accuracy across the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do weak-ratio baselines and matched stronger-ratio probes preserve the same completion tail within each scaffold family?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount, loading-solvent volume, and mobile-phase ratio interact non-smoothly, with V2 sometimes changing much more than V1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched condition contrasts expose interactions that cannot be learned reliably from structure-only similarity or isolated labels.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed scaffold, do loading and ratio shifts move onset and completion together, or mainly create a V2 tail?

hypotheses.content: Basic and acceptor-rich aromatic structures form a transferable but condition-sensitive failure region, while simple nitrile, halogen, and other acceptor controls can remain compact.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model needs structural-condition interactions that distinguish basic aromatic adsorption from generic aromaticity or acceptor count.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do amino aromatic esters and fused nitrogen structures show the same condition threshold as the measured pyridyl and benzophenone failures?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing aromatic structures have scaffold-specific retention tails; donor count alone does not determine whether the response is compact or delayed.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Donor-family controls teach attachment geometry and flexibility effects instead of forcing a global HBD correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which donor-containing aromatic scaffolds switch from compact elution to delayed completion as ratio or loading changes?

hypotheses.content: Some aromatic ketone and ester families show threshold-like onset changes with solvent strength, with V1 and V2 not necessarily scaling proportionally.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Same-molecule ratio contrasts can teach separate onset and completion responses and improve interpolation between sparse condition levels.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched hydrophobic ketone and fused-hydrocarbon contrasts show a reproducible onset threshold while completion remains compact?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback reinforced localized endpoint behavior. The m177 measurements showed a compact V2 at 100 ul but a very large V2 at 150 ul under the same 50/1 ratio, while m125 and m199 also showed severe condition-dependent completion tails. Compact outcomes for heavy-halogen and weakly interacting rows such as m140, m152, and m136 weakened any global V2 inflation rule. The batch therefore emphasizes compact anchors, same-molecule or same-family condition contrasts, and structural controls around basic, carbonyl, donor, and ester failure regions.
batch_rationale: The 32 candidates combine compact hydrophobic and heavy-atom anchors with several meaningful local contrasts: m152, m147, and m12 each provide paired conditions, while aromatic ketones, esters, amino esters, alcohols, aldehydes, and multi-carbonyl structures cover distinct interaction classes. The batch samples PE and DCM, weak to strong ratios, multiple sample volumes, and loading-solvent amounts. These labels should repair known boundary failures, teach endpoint-specific response curves, and constrain calibration for ordinary rows, improving generalization across both compact and delayed regions of the Row-distribution.
